EXCLUSIVE: Sandy Liang Partners With F1 Academy and Amex on Limited-Edition Capsule Collection
article_text:
As a Formula 1 fan since 2020, Sandy Liang‘s latest partnership with F1 Academy and American Express on a limited capsule collection for the upcoming Vegas Grand Prix is a “dream come true.”

The capsule collection features hoodies, hats, long-sleeved T-shirts, scarves and a hat with the brand’s signature feminine motifs of bows, sparkles and stars graphic designs.

“It’s my first time making sports merch,” Liang told WWD. “It was important for me to create pieces you’d actually keep wearing after the race, not just at the track. It’s very much the Sandy girl going to the Grand Prix. We wanted to bring that same cute and fun aesthetic into the merch collection.”

Moreover, she said putting her artwork and graphics on a blank slate was a fun way to imagine herself as a different customer — one who’s at the racetrack or in the merchandise store and gearing up for what to wear to the race. Different from her normal process and consumer, she thinks of the merchandise as being more so “memorabilia.”

“I love collaborating and working on projects that are not clothes directly. I love the sport and I love cars in general. This was really fun to know that a crazy piece of technology has my design. It’s the duality of girlie but strong and fast.”

Alongside the capsule collection, the designer also designed a livery and helmet for F1 Academy driver Ava Dobson. Another first for Liang, she said her vision was rooted in themes of nostalgia and girlhood. (She also looked to previous cars’ livery and was inspired by the “amazing women” in the sport.)

“The livery was inspired by Sailor Moon, especially her transformation, and the idea of the car being wrapped like a present with ribbons streaming behind it. ”

Liang’s entry into the motorsport came via Netflix’s “Drive to Survive,” with the drama behind the scenes of the sport and learning more about the drivers, which made her “fall in love” with Formula 1. Three races she has attended in the past are Montreal, Austin and Las Vegas. The New York designer also considers herself a “diehard” Lewis Hamilton fan.

“Formula 1 has become such an important part of our global sponsorship portfolio. We’re always looking for ways to give our card members unique access and experiences while also supporting the continued growth of the sport. F1 Academy is a great example of that and we’re proud to support a platform that’s broadening opportunity and helping shape the future of Formula 1,” said Shiz Suzuki, vice president of global brand sponsorships and experiential marketing at American Express.

The Sandy Liang x F1 Academy x American Express collection retails from $78 to $108 and is available exclusively to American Express card members at the F1 Las Vegas Hub throughout November and during the race weekend, Thursday through Saturday.

title: Emails Show Administrators Seeking To Have Protections For Non-Revenue Sports Stripped From PCSA
article_text:
On July 10, University of Oklahoma President Joseph Harroz Jr. emailed Southeastern Conference Commissioner Greg Sankey and leaders of the other 15 SEC universities, urging the conference to prioritize stripping protections for Olympic sports from the Protect College Sports Act. “The current restrictions on Olympic sport sponsorship, funding, and scheduling should be removed,” he wrote. Schools needed flexibility to “respond to consumer demand.”

If the conference could not resolve the issues together, Harroz said he would address them “from Oklahoma’s perspective.” Action was necessary, he warned, as schools should expect “another unbudgeted increase of $10+ million” in football roster costs next year.

University of Mississippi Chancellor Glenn Boyce responded the next day, saying he agreed with Harroz.

Sankey sent SEC presidents an updated talking points memo on July 13. Co-authored with the Big Ten and titled “Common Sense Improvements for the Protect College Sports Act,” it was already being shared with Senate offices, he told them. The memo called scholarship and roster requirements for women’s and Olympic sports “unfunded mandates.” Schools, the conferences argued, needed “flexibility to preserve opportunities across all sports while remaining financially responsible.”

These documents, obtained by Defector through public records requests requests to the University of Texas, Texas A&M University, and the University of Washington, show that while the Big Ten and SEC had previously argued in public for congressional intervention in order to preserve athletic opportunities in women’s and Olympic sports, they were seeking in private to have requirements for funding those sports stripped from the final version of the PCSA.

David Bassity, the Big Ten’s Senior Vice President of Communications, responded on behalf of the Big Ten to Defector. The Big Ten said its objection was to having scholarship and roster decisions “micromanaged in federal legislation.” The conference said its schools had added hundreds of scholarships outside football and basketball, mostly in women’s sports, and reiterated its support for the PCSA.

Harroz and the SEC did not respond to Defector’s request for comment.

Months before Harroz, Sankey, and Boyce sent those emails, the conferences had repeatedly made protecting non-revenue sports part of their case for Congress to intervene on college sports. After a White House roundtable on March 6, Sankey and Big Ten Commissioner Tony Petitti joined their ACC and Big 12 counterparts in calling for policies that “protect women’s and Olympic programs.” They endorsed the SCORE Act, a separate college sports bill that originated in the House of Representatives.

Petitti made the point again on April 3. Responding to President Donald Trump’s executive order on college sports, he praised the SCORE Act for “protecting academic and athletic opportunities provided through women’s and Olympic sports programs.”

House leaders pulled the SCORE Act from a vote on May 18. The bill has since stalled in the House. Nine days after it was pulled, Sens. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) and Maria Cantwell (D-Wash) unveiled the PCSA.

The June 15 update to the PCSA added Section 125, which set out protections for women’s and Olympic sports. Schools with at least $80 million in annual athletics revenue would have to maintain scholarship levels in non-revenue sports at the 2024–25 baseline.

Chad Hawley, the Big Ten’s senior vice president for policy, asked universities in states with senators on the Senate Commerce Committee to send a template letter on June 17. The letter said they could not support the June 15 revision.

It called Section 125’s scholarship protections “an unfunded mandate that removes institutional decision-making authority” and warned that the provision would have “a disproportionate negative impact on institutions like those in the Big Ten that have provided the most opportunities and support in women’s and Olympic sports.”

On July 13, the NCAA urged its members to contact senators in support of the bill. Hawley forwarded the message to university government relations officials with instructions to “disregard the NCAA office’s call to action for now.” The conference’s position remained unchanged, he wrote: “the problems with the bill are such that it cannot be supported in its current form.”

On July 26, Brad Grantz, the Senate Commerce Committee’s Republican staff director, sent an email to Sankey and Petitti outlining concessions Washington had made to garner support from both conferences. Grantz called it a “substantial package” and said he hoped the conferences would now be “part of the solution.”

The material Grantz sent specifically listed “Flexibility on Mandate for Olympic and Non-Revenue Sports” as a request from the conferences. It outlined the concession this way: “Institutions can modify or substitute the sports that are sponsored or the number of roster spots and scholarships provided for each sports [sic], provided that the total number of scholarship and roster spots remains at or above the baseline.”

In other words, schools could now use an aggregate number of scholarships to satisfy the PCSA’s mandate, rather than having them be tied to individual sports.

The conferences’ own documents suggest why the bill sponsors thought the change would appease the SEC and Big Ten, even if the larger ask of getting rid of the mandate entirely wasn’t met. A co-authored document specifically mentioned the conferences were looking into adding flag football as a new sport to sponsor in the future.

Flag football could offer a considerably cheaper option. A study commissioned by the University of California, Davis, projected first-year expenses of about $316,000, including scholarships and coaching. Georgia’s financial report for fiscal year 2024 listed annual operating expenses of $3.6 million for gymnastics, $3.4 million for equestrian, and $2.3 million for women’s swimming and diving.

title: Adobe continues AI-focused partnerships with US SailGP Team
article_text:
The US team from the international SailGP series has announced a new global partnership with software giant Adobe.

Through the agreement, the US-based company will serve as the team’s official AI fan experience partner.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The US SailGP Team will utilize Adobe’s marketing and AI-powered tools, such as Adobe CX Enterprise, for customer experience orchestration.

Adobe’s AI-powered technology will be embedded across the U.S. SailGP Team’s content operation and fan journey.

The software firm’s creative tools will support how the team captures, creates, and distributes content from race weekends, while its AI marketing and customer experience orchestration capabilities will enable the team to “deliver more relevant experiences based on how fans engage.”

Mike Buckley, team principal, CEO and co-owner of the US SailGP Team, said: “From day one, we’ve built this team to compete at the highest level in everything we do on the water and off it.

“We’ve relied on Adobe products to tell our story for years, so this partnership supercharges something already deeply embedded in how our team works. Great storytelling is part of how we build our brand and connect with our fans, and now we have an opportunity to take that even further together.”

The partnership will focus on AI innovations including content production, personalized fan experiences, and discoverability across AI surfaces.

The US SailGP Team will have access to various tools such as Adobe GenStudio, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Real-Time CDP, Adobe CX Analytics, Adobe Journey Optimizer, Adobe Brand Visibility, and Adobe Experience Manager Assets.

The team said the partnership is part of its wider strategy to create a modern sports brand. In 2023 the team became the first franchise in SailGP history to bring in a private equity investor, with Avenue Sports Fund leading the acquisition.

As well as its global partner and official AI fan experience partner designations, Adobe will have branding on the F50 catamaran and team kit across the SailGP season, integration into the team’s content production and creative workflows, co-branded storytelling and campaign opportunities, premium hospitality, and access to the team’s network of partners, investors, and SailGP’s broader institutional community.

Olli Coupe, managing director of Adobe Private Capital, added: “The US SailGP Team has an ambitious plan for engaging and growing its fanbase, and Adobe’s AI-powered technology will play a role in driving that forward.

“Today’s sailing fans expect experiences that are personal and connected on and beyond race day. This partnership gives us an exciting platform to bring Adobe’s creative and AI marketing capabilities into sport and create new ways to connect its fans, partners, and investors to the action.”

Adobe has unveiled several AI-focused partnerships in sports in recent weeks. Last month, the company was named the official AI fan experience partner of the Alpine Formula 1 motor racing team and the AI marketing and creativity partner of the Australian Open tennis Grand Slam.

The Australian Open deal marks the company's first entry into tennis.

title: Premier League gambling advertising ban falls short of full compliance
article_text:
The English Premier League has moved away from bookmaker logos on the front of playing shirts from the 2026/27 season. However, gambling advertising has not disappeared from broadcast coverage. Research from the University of Bristol found that the measure reduced the overall volume of advertising messages by only around 10%, with approximately half of that reduction offset by increased exposure on sleeves, training kits, and pitchside LED boards.

The viewing experience has changed only minimally in practice. Thousands of betting brand references continue to accompany every match, casting doubt on the real effectiveness of the voluntary restriction and fuelling debate about the need for stricter regulation.

Modern gambling entertainment, which includes sports betting, is growing more popular every year. This covers everything from slots and poker to live shows with real dealers. According to data available here, Monopoly Live by Evolution and similar games have become genuine hits over the past several months.

The popularity of these products is linked to the fact that British audiences have a fondness for enjoying live game shows, and not only gambling formats. The iGaming industry in the country therefore strives to match local tastes, which helps it remain successful. Sports betting, naturally, is also a long-standing British tradition, which is why its advertising continues despite resistance from authorities.

The ban is narrowly constructed and applies exclusively to the front of playing shirts. All other space has remained open to bookmakers. The following formats are permitted:

A source who had worked on commercial contracts between betting operators and clubs explained to Front Office Sports that for a global audience “the front of the shirt is prestigious, but LED boards matter most for those watching matches around the world.” It is the constant visibility of pitchside advertising that delivers maximum reach, rather than a static logo on a player’s chest.

Betting operators’ interest in English football is driven by direct conversion. Sean Connell, editor of industry consultancy The Sponsor, notes that “bookmakers need enormous volumes of brand awareness,” and club sponsorship creates “a fairly direct link between the logo on the shirt and the number of newly registered customers.” The male Premier League audience aligns with the core target demographic of betting operators, and no better vehicle for this category simply exists.

The pioneer was Betfair, which signed a deal with Fulham in 2002. Within a decade, three-quarters of Premier League clubs were carrying bookmaker logos. According to a source close to several deals, betting operators paid roughly twice as much as rivals from other industries, and this generosity created a deep financial dependency on the category among clubs.

Political pressure built gradually. In 2020, a House of Lords committee described the regulation of the gambling industry as “soft” and recommended a complete ban on sports sponsorship by bookmakers. The Premier League adopted a pre-emptive approach and in 2023 announced a voluntary phased withdrawal of bookmaker logos from the front of shirts, with a three-year transition period. The government, in turn, signalled that it would not tighten shirt rules if the league managed the process itself.

Half of Premier League clubs had to find new front-of-shirt sponsors last summer. Bournemouth expanded its agreement with insurance company Vitality, Brentford added a playing shirt to its contract with recruitment platform Indeed, and Nottingham Forest signed a last-minute deal with financial firm Marex. Sunderland and Chelsea began the season without a front-of-shirt sponsor at all, though Chelsea subsequently signed a contract with crypto company Circle.

According to estimates by Ampere Analytics analyst Adam Lewis, the eight clubs that changed partners grew the combined annual value of their front-of-shirt contracts from $89m (£67m) to $99m (£75m). At the same time, the combined value of sleeve and training kit deals rose from $176m (£133m) to $206m (£156m), with a significant portion of bookmaker money migrating into these permitted areas. The bookmakers’ share of training kit sponsorships is estimated to have exceeded 50%.

The ban applies only at Premier League level. Clubs in the three lower divisions retain the right to sign deals with betting operators, and the government concluded that a full ban risked devastating the finances of dozens of clubs. In addition, bookmaker brands are visible in UEFA competitions held at English grounds. Betano, the former sponsor of Aston Villa, is the lead partner of the Europa League, the Conference League, and the upcoming Euro 2028 in the United Kingdom and Ireland.

Against the backdrop of restrictions on traditional bookmakers, attention is shifting to prediction markets, which could potentially attempt to circumvent the definition of “gambling.” The leading platforms Polymarket and Kalshi do not yet operate legally in the United Kingdom, but the Premier League’s global reach makes sponsorship attractive for promotion in overseas markets. The Premier League stated that it “cannot comment on whether prediction market operators would fall under the existing rule.” The Gambling Commission is more sceptical, taking the view that such an operator would be unlikely to classify itself as a “non-gambling” product on UK territory.

A European precedent has already been set. An Italian court this summer struck down Polymarket’s $21m (€19m) contract with Lazio, ruling that such platforms fall under the gambling sponsorship ban. In England, regulation is softer thanks to the league’s self-regulatory approach, and the question remains open. The decisive moment will come with the first real contract and the regulator’s response.

title: DFL appoints HBS’ Wistuba to lead Sportcast brodacast production
article_text:
German soccer’s DFL league organizer has announced the appointment of experienced sports broadcast director Stefan Wistuba as the new chief executive (CEO) of its in-house production arm, Sportcast.

Wistuba will join the Sportcast managing board (which unanimously selected him for the role) on May 1, 2027, for a transitionary period before taking over the CEO role in full on June 30, replacing the outgoing Josef Nehl.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Nehl is retiring after what will be a 21-year stint at the helm of Sportcast, having overseen operations at the business since it was founded.

Speaking on the leadership shift, Sportcast supervisory board chair and Bundesliga chief executive Steffen Merkel said: “Josef Nehl has not only led Sportcast for more than two decades, but has also built up the company since its foundation and played a decisive role in shaping it.

“With his vast experience, high standards of quality and keen sense of technological developments, he has made a significant contribution to raising the media production of the Bundesliga and Bundesliga 2 to the very highest international standards.

“In Stefan Wistuba, we have also found the right successor to continue this successful development and to further advance Sportcast within a dynamically changing media and technology landscape.

Sportcast, which was created in 2006, oversees the TV production of all top-flight Bundesliga and second-tier 2. Bundesliga matches, as well as all games in the DFB Pokal knockout tournament and the Super Cup, and coordinates international broadcast signal distribution for rights holders in over 200 countries.

Wistuba joins from Host Broadcast Services (HBS), the television production company owned by international sports marketing agency Infront, after 18 years at the organization.

He joined HBS in August 2028 as production and project manager for a range of its contracted FIFA soccer tournaments, including the FIFA World Cup 2010 in South Africa, and the FIFA Women's World Cup 2011 in Germany.

Following that, he took up similar production management roles for the FIFA World Cups in 2014 (Brazil) and 2018 (Russia), as well as the 2015 Women’s World Cup (Canada), before becoming head of production in 2017.

Wistuba eventually rose to the role of director of production (2019 to 2024), and is now the director of the FIFA projects unit, having also been the project director for the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the US, Canada, and Mexico, which featured more games than any previous World Cup.

In his new role, he will work alongside incumbent Sportscast managing director Alexander Günther.

Merkel continued: “Stefan Wistuba has many years of experience and proven expertise in the media and production sectors, as well as a strong spirit of innovation. Together with Alexander Günther and the entire team, he will successfully drive Sportcast’s development forward and provide important impetus for the company’s future.”

title: Revolut under judicial administration: what is at stake for its Audi F1 sponsorship
article_text:
In my view, in the short term, almost nothing. On 16 November 2026 a Milan court placed the Italian branch of Revolut, the bank that gives its name to the Audi Revolut F1 Team, under judicial administration for one year. The court granted the request of the Milan public prosecutor’s office, which alleges serious shortcomings in the bank’s anti-money-laundering controls. The bank stays open, though, and the order is not a conviction: that is why I believe Audi will leave the contract alone. The real risk lies in communications, because for a bank the product is trust.

Suppose you are the head of communications at a Formula 1 team. One morning the name written on your car is in the headlines for a reason that has nothing to do with overtaking. What do you do? Do you take the logo off before the next race? Do you ring the sponsor to find out what it is going to say? Do you put out a statement? Or do you wait, hoping the story slides down the page?

Formula 1 has been here before, more often than you might think. Motorsport has always had a soft spot for people who handle money: banks, finance houses, cryptocurrency platforms, people who love speed almost as much as we do. Every so often, though, one of them comes under a judge’s scrutiny, and the answers given over the years say a good deal about what to expect now.

What did the Milan court decide about Revolut?

On 16 November 2026 the preventive measures section of the Court of Milan ordered one year of judicial administration for the Italian branch of Revolut Bank, the Revolut group’s Lithuanian bank. The order was requested by the Milan public prosecutor’s office and carried out by the Guardia di Finanza, Italy’s financial police.

The issue is anti-money-laundering controls. For anyone who does not work in a bank, these are the checks a bank must carry out to understand who its customers are and where their money comes from. According to prosecutors, Revolut’s controls in Italy were so weak that people under investigation, or already convicted, were able to use the bank’s accounts. Some of them are alleged to have links to organised crime, and tens of millions of euros are alleged to have passed through those accounts. The criminal investigations concern these customers; the measure imposed on the bank is there to fix the controls.

Revolut has said that it acknowledges the decision, that it will cooperate fully with the Italian authorities and that its banking services in Italy continue to operate normally, with no interruption for customers. This is not the first time someone has taken a close look at its controls. In April 2025 the Bank of Lithuania fined Revolut Bank €3.5 million for shortcomings in the monitoring of customer transactions.

Judicial administration: what does it mean for a bank that sponsors Formula 1?

It means that for one year the bank works with two court-appointed administrators at its side, who check and correct its procedures. It is a preventive measure under article 34 of Italy’s anti-mafia code (Legislative Decree 159/2011): it does not establish criminal guilt and it does not close the company, which carries on operating. The sponsor, in other words, carries on doing its job.

The Court of Milan has already used this measure on some very well-known companies. In April 2024 it was the turn of Giorgio Armani Operations, and in June of Manufactures Dior, over a failure to check suppliers where labour exploitation had come to light. In both cases the measure was lifted in February 2025, ahead of schedule, after the companies had overhauled their controls.

The case closest to Revolut’s, because it involves a bank, is that of Banca Progetto. In October 2024 the court placed it under judicial administration over loans granted to companies linked to a person arrested in 2023 in an investigation into the ‘Ndrangheta. In July 2025 the measure was lifted early. In the meantime, however, in March 2025 the Bank of Italy, the country’s central bank, had put it into special administration under a separate order: the court lifting its measure did not put an end to the bank’s problems.

For Revolut, in my view, these are the precedents that matter, far more than the Formula 1 ones we will come to in a moment. They tell us two things: that a measure like this can be closed early, and that the court is not the only referee. How it ends will depend on what the administrators find and on how quickly the bank puts things right.

When a financial sponsor has run into trouble, how have Formula 1 teams handled the communications?

In three different ways. As I see it, the choice almost always came down to a single question: can the sponsor still pay, and is it still presentable? When the answer was no, the team cut ties within hours. When it was yes, the team either managed the exit or carried on regardless. On the blog you will also find six F1 sponsorships that failed and the story of crypto sponsorship, from the boom to the collapse of FTX.

On 11 November 2022 FTX, the cryptocurrency platform that sponsored Mercedes, filed for bankruptcy protection in the United States. That same day Mercedes suspended the deal, and at the Brazilian Grand Prix the cars raced without the logo. Toto Wolff said that “partners like us” had been left in “utter disbelief”. “We considered FTX,” he said, “because they were one of the most credible and solid, financially sound partners that were out there.” The matter did not end there. In November 2023 a group of investors sued the company behind the team, accusing it of promoting unregistered financial products without checking closely enough who it was promoting. As far as is known, there is still no ruling that concerns the team.

title: International Swimming League agrees global rights deal with DAZN
article_text:
The International Swimming League (ISL), the club-based professional series, has announced a global media rights agreement with major sports streaming platform DAZN.

Through the agreement, DAZN will be responsible for the worldwide distribution of the league's upcoming relaunch event, the ISL All-Star Match.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The one-night event takes place at the London Aquatics Centre in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park on December 19.

The All-Star Match will be live and free globally on DAZN, in English, on a non-exclusive basis, outside several reserved territories where dedicated local broadcast arrangements will be announced separately.

DAZN will broadcast the event across its 200 markets.

The All-Star Match will see the world's fastest swimmers compete in a team-based, two-hour, head-to-head competition.

Four teams will compete, based on a geographical principle: the United States, the Commonwealth, Europe, and the rest of the world, each made up of the leading athletes from their region.

The ISL will unveil further broadcast and distribution partners “in the coming weeks.”

Ben Allen, commissioner of the International Swimming League, said: “The All-Star Match is built to be watched, and this agreement means fans almost anywhere in the world can do so live and free.

“DAZN is the home of some of the biggest sports on the planet, and swimming’s return to the ISL stage belongs in that company.”

Last month, the ISL appointed Gravity Media as its broadcast content and production partner ahead of its relaunch.

The ISL’s comeback campaign will see as many as seven fixtures staged in venues across North America, Europe, Asia, and potentially the Middle East next year.

It will feature a refined format, with the trial of a one-day event concept, as opposed to the prior two-day edition.

Late last year, ISL commissioner Ben Allen explained that this relaunch will come with a revamped commercial and funding model aimed at ensuring the sustainability of the series, which was suspended in 2022 after the Russian invasion of Ukraine, which hampered the business interests of primary investor Konstantin Grigorishin.

Grigorishin, the founder and chair of the ISL, remains involved, but the series is also now drawing on a wider range of revenue streams, particularly sponsorship and broadcast income, to ensure its commercial model is more balanced going forward, and to further insulate it from geopolitical shocks such as the war in Ukraine and the COVID-19 pandemic.

The series was initially conceived as a means of maintaining interest in swimming annually outside of the Olympics.

In its initial iteration, the ISL attracted high-profile names such as Olympic champions Adam Peaty and Katinka Hosszú, but those same swimmers have also been mired in lawsuits related to antitrust concerns against the World Aquatics governing body.

It faced a legal dispute with FINA (now World Aquatics) during 2018 and 2019, with the governing body having initially refused to allow athletes to compete in it as an unsanctioned series and then launching its own direct competitor.

As with other sports around the world, the ISL then faced disruption during 2020, its second season, because of the coronavirus pandemic, as well as further associated legal difficulties.

With the lawsuits seemingly settled and new backing secured, a roadmap for the return of the ISL was created.

Allen also stated his hope that the momentum surrounding the LA28 Olympic Games and swimming’s position at the games could help to bolster interest in the series.

Karren Brady and Nathan Thompson launch sports agency
article_text:
Former West Ham United Vice-Chairman Baroness Karren Brady CBE has joined forces with Nathan Thompson to launch Brady Thompson, a new agency aiming to unlock hundreds of millions of pounds in untapped commercial value across UK sport and entertainment.

The agency will focus on three areas: originating and securing high-value commercial partnerships, transforming corporate hospitality and its revenue potential, and advising brands on strategy across sport and entertainment.

Brady brings decades of boardroom experience across sport, entertainment, media and business. As well as her time at West Ham, she is a Member of the House of Lords and Lord Sugar’s business adviser on the BBC’s The Apprentice.

Thompson is a senior executive and board-level leader whose experience spans sponsorship, brand partnerships, venues, marketing and commercial development. When he left West Ham, he was one of only two Black board members in the Premier League.

Baroness Karren Brady CBE, Co-Founder of Brady Thompson, said, “Sport and entertainment have never been more commercially powerful. Audiences are global, brands are increasingly recognising the value of being part of that world, and the commercial opportunities are enormous. Yet there remains a significant gap between the value organisations are currently generating and what they could achieve.“

She adds,“Unlocking that potential takes more than simply selling sponsorship or hospitality. It takes commercial imagination, experience, relationships, the right processes and, above all, the bravery to challenge convention. That is what Brady Thompson is here to deliver.”

The agency launches as rights holders face growing pressure to maximise their commercial assets, while brands look for more sophisticated ways to connect with audiences. Its approach centres on identifying opportunities others overlook and turning them into measurable commercial outcomes.

Nathan Thompson, Co-Founder of Brady Thompson, said, “I’ve sat in boardrooms on every side of these deals – as a sales executive, an adviser and a board member. title: British Cycling Ventures and Koru team up
article_text:
British Cycling Ventures has formed a joint venture with Koru Sports Group to drive the commercial growth of the City of London Nocturne, with plans to take the closed-road race to more UK cities.

The event returns on 11th-12th June 2027 at the Square Mile Race Circuit, a 1.4km course that winds through Cheapside and Bank with the Royal Exchange and the City skyline as its backdrop. Elite day and night racing runs alongside a street party of live music, food stalls and entertainment, with riders of all ages and abilities taking part.

The 2026 edition was broadcast live and featured a family-friendly programme including the Penny Farthing Race, the Brompton Folding Bike Race and the new Voi Bike Challenge.

The venture aims to expand the Nocturne nationally and give teams and riders new opportunities, while complementing the domestic racing structure, including the Lloyds National Circuit Series. It will focus on fan experience, new audiences in key urban markets and a strong commercial programme.

The move follows growing momentum for cycling in the UK. Thousands of fans lined the streets for this year’s Lloyds Tour of Britain Women and Men, and tickets for December’s UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup in Glasgow have been in high demand.

Darren Henry, Managing Director of British Cycling Ventures, said, “This is another significant moment in the major events vision of British Cycling Ventures, and the commercial growth of major city racing in the UK. “

“The innovation and plans for growth of the Nocturne from Koru Sports Group is significant for cycling in the country, and this joint venture brings together the best expertise in our sport to deliver huge impact through high-quality events. After hosting a brilliant event in the heart of London this year, it will continue to produce a spectacular atmosphere for riders and fans alike and make it an event not to be missed.”

James Pope of Koru Sports Group said, “I’ve been privileged to have been organising cycling events for over two decades in the UK and have worked closely with British Cycling during this time. The plans and ambition of British Cycling Ventures present an exciting opportunity to introduce a new major city racing concept in the UK starting with the City of London Nocturne. This partnership will help us create a new world class city event format that will be a major boost to the UK racing scene, creating a fantastic experience for riders and cycling fans.”

title: Cadillac F1 signs Viatris as pharmaceutical partner
article_text:
The Cadillac Formula 1 Team, which ran its debut season from its base at Silverstone, has signed healthcare company Viatris to a multi-year partnership starting in 2027.

Although Cadillac is billed as America’s new Formula 1 team, Silverstone is at the heart of its operation. While construction of its US headquarters in Fishers, Indiana, is completed, the team has run its 2026 campaign mainly from the Northamptonshire facility. The base houses its logistics as well as its aerodynamic and mechanical design. The team has committed to keeping the facility for at least ten years, giving it access to the experienced talent of the UK’s Motorsport Valley.

Viatris will become the team’s global pharmaceutical partner from the 2027 season, Cadillac’s second on the grid. The partnership links motorsport and medicine, two industries where precision, reliability and performance matter.

Viatris marks its sixth anniversary this year. It was formed in 2020 through the combination of Mylan and Upjohn, a former division of Pfizer, and has since delivered medicines to patients in more than 165 countries and territories. Its portfolio covers generics, value-added medicines, established brands and innovative medicines.

Viatris’s UK business is headquartered in Hatfield, Hertfordshire, and supplies medicines to patients across the country.

Tyler Epp, Global Head of Commercial Strategy at Cadillac Formula 1 Team, said, “Viatris makes medicines that people count on every day, and Formula 1® gives them one of the biggest stages in the world to show how they do it. For a team in its first season, having a global company like Viatris choose to partner with the Cadillac Formula 1® Team says a lot about where we’re headed. We are thankful for the trust that Viatris has placed in our team and cannot wait to grow with them into the future.”

Andrew Enrietti, Chief Administrative and Transformation Officer at Viatris, said, “What attracted us to the Cadillac Formula 1® Team is the ambition and ingenuity behind what they’re building. At Viatris, we’re focused on executing our strategy and continuing to find ways to make a difference for patients around the world.“

“We share a determination to embrace new opportunities, bring talented people and different perspectives together, and turn bold ideas into meaningful progress. This partnership gives us an exciting opportunity to showcase that shared spirit while introducing Viatris to new audiences around the world.”

Viatris joins the group of global companies that partnered with the team in its first season. The team is backed by TWG Motorsports and General Motors, and its wider commercial programme will grow as the Fishers headquarters opens in 2027. It aims to become a full-works American team by the end of the decade. Excel Sports Management, the team’s agency of record, supported the partnership discussions.

title: Ezpeleta: MotoGP valued ‘reach before fees’ in ESPN deal
article_text:
MotoGP is prioritising reach over rights fees with its new US broadcast deal with ESPN, according to the series’ deputy chief executive Carlos Ezpeleta.

Last week, the global motorcycling series signed a two-year media rights deal with the Disney-owned broadcaster across the US and Latin America. This is MotoGP’s first broadcast deal in the former since its takeover by Liberty Media.

Beginning in 2027, MotoGP races will air on ESPN networks and platforms in the United States, either live or on same-day delay. Across Latin America, ESPN will continue to provide extensive MotoGP coverage, including streaming on Disney+.

MotoGP has partnered with ESPN in Latin America since 2002 and this new agreement also enables the broadcaster so sublicense select events in Argentina and Brazil to local free-to-air broadcasters.

However, the US market is still underdeveloped for MotoGP. Ezpeleta told SportsPro that the first priority is “to just get our wonderful sport in front of more eyeballs”.

He added: “The most important thing that we valued in this deal and in this market is just reach before fees. … Investments in a sport come in many shapes and sizes, and picking the best possible media partners is one of those investments, sometimes it’s picking visibility and reach.”

The short-term nature of the deal also ensures MotoGP can properly evaluate the market before renegotiating for the 2029 season and beyond.

“In a more mature market, you need more time to actually make a significant change in percentage,” said Ezpeleta. “We’re going into ESPN without knowing what that bar is. So again, we have our own numbers but we’re sure that it will be a success.”

ESPN was Formula One’s media rights partner in the US before its transition to Apple TVthis season, so having that industry knowledge from within Liberty helped the negotiation process.

“[Liberty chief executive] Derek Chang knows everybody at ESPN, and then of course we have on our board Chase Carey and Sean Bratches, so all of those people are very well known to ESPN,” confirmed Ezpeleta.

“Obviously, the deals always have to make sense from a negotiation standpoint, but being able to leverage those voices and really getting that buy-in from ESPN is very valuable.”

At the same time, Ezpeleta is clear that MotoGP is trying to do things its own way. While the series is technically following the Formula One playbook in the US, the Spaniard maintained that “MotoGP and Formula One are two different brands”.

Ezpeleta also confirmed that VideoPass will still be available to the US market despite this new deal with ESPN as the US “is actually our biggest single market for VideoPass” and ESPN will be more focused on providing top-of-funnel access.

And looking to the future, Ezpeleta is hopeful that a successful media rights deal will lead to more race opportunities for MotoGP in the US.

“Long term we would be looking to add when the time is right, and especially when the destination is right, a destination within the US that’s additive, that’s reaching a different type of fan,” he said.

Until then, success will be measured by the number of eyeballs drawn to the sport, something Ezpeleta hopes will then “transfer to success in all of our revenue streams”.

title: Stena Line and Special Olympics Ireland Mark First Year of Partnership
article_text:
Stena Line and Special Olympics Ireland marked the first anniversary of their partnership by celebrating the athletes, volunteers and communities supported through the sponsorship over the past 12 months.

The partnership was launched in November 2025 and is built around a shared belief in the power of sport to change lives and create greater inclusion.

To mark the anniversary, Stena Line crew welcomed three Special Olympics Ireland athletes onboard Stena Estrid, where they joined broadcaster Marie Crowe in reflecting on what the partnership has meant to them.

Each was asked to choose one word to describe the relationship, with empowerment, togetherness, equality and opportunity among those selected.

Stena Line captain Master Jack Deurden chose “inspiring”, highlighting the impact that meeting Special Olympics athletes has had on the ship’s crew.

“It’s a pleasure for us to meet the athletes, to welcome them onboard and show them around the ship,” he said.

“The dedication and resilience they display really is inspiring, and it’s great to be able to have a chat with them, learn a bit about their journey and understand what it takes for these athletes and their families to achieve what they have.”

Special Olympics Ireland athlete Carrie Doyle said the organisation had played an important role in building her own confidence.

“The Special Olympics has taught me to be a stronger person and has improved my confidence.

“I would like to thank Stena Line for welcoming us on board, showing us the beautiful boat and for listening to us talk about our experience.”

Stena Line’s support is helping Special Olympics Ireland provide almost 7,000 athletes across the island with access to training, competition and personal development opportunities, from local club activity through to representing Ireland internationally.

The partnership played a visible role at this year’s Special Olympics Ireland Summer Games. Over 1,200 athletes and 2,500 volunteers took part in the largest inclusive sports event staged here since the World Games in 2003.

Stena Line supported the recruitment and deployment of those volunteers without whom the Games would not have been possible.

Johan Edelman, Trade Director for Stena Line, said the first year had reinforced the values shared by both organisations.

“We’re honoured to support Special Olympics Ireland and play a part in the journey of these incredible athletes as they make a real difference in local communities across Ireland.

“We’ve been inspired by the dedication and hard work they have displayed throughout the past 12 months.

“Inclusivity and care are an important part of the Stena Line way, and the Special Olympics Ireland Summer Games were incredible.

“We’re all excited to see the athletes prepare for the Special Olympics World Summer Games in Santiago, Chile next year.”

“Partnerships like this go far beyond funding sport; they change lives, strengthen communities, and champion inclusion across Ireland,” said Karen Coventry, CEO of Special Olympics Ireland.

“We are deeply grateful to Stena Line for their continued support and for being such an important part of this journey.”

The partnership provides sponsorship that supports the impact which the Special Olympics has across the country.

It also delivers moments of inspiration for the company and its staff that are hard to put a value on.

title: Defending champs TKR secure boost for CPL as bpTT steps up
article_text:
Five-time champions and defending titleholders Trinbago Knight Riders (TKR) have secured major backing for the upcoming Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League (CPL) season, officially locking in bp Trinidad and Tobago (bpTT) as a key sponsor.

The historic partnership was sealed on Tuesday at a signing ceremony at the Hyatt Regency, Port-of-Spain, marking the energy giant’s first-ever national-level sports sponsorship of this scale.

TKR enter the 2026 campaign riding high as the CPL's most successful franchise, aiming to add a sixth star to their chest. The alliance with bpTT brings powerful local backing to the team as they prepare to battle the region’s best on cricket’s biggest regional stage.

"bpTT is committed to supporting sport, culture and national pride in T&T," said David Campbell, President of bp Latin America and the Caribbean. "We are honoured to come on board as a sponsor of the Trinbago Knight Riders. TKR’s success is based on dedication and a commitment to excellence–qualities that align to our values at bp. We are looking forward to accompanying TKR on their journey to defend their CPL title."

For bpTT, the deal marks a bold expansion of its sports investment strategy. The sponsorship builds on bpTT’s long-standing support for sport, particularly in their fenceline community of Mayaro and Guayaguayare, and represents an expansion of that commitment to a wider national platform.

Coinciding with bpTT’s 65th anniversary of operations in Trinidad and Tobago, company representatives noted that partnering with TKR reflects six and a half decades of shared values, passion, and national pride.

With the 2026 CPL season fast approaching, the defending champions now have the backing of one of the country's biggest corporate giants as they set their sights on back-to-back glory.

title: Sports Entertainment Group Launches Adelaide Broadcast Precinct SEN SA House with AAMI Naming Rights
article_text:
Sports Entertainment Group (SEG) has announced a capital investment to establish SEN SA House, a state-of-the-art sports media and broadcast precinct at 1 King William Street on the corner of North Terrace in Adelaide’s central business district.

Announced on 16 November 2026 to mark SEN SA’s eighth anniversary, the development is backed by a three-year naming-rights partnership with Australian insurer AAMI. Scheduled for completion in late 2026, the facility sits within walking distance of Adelaide Oval and aims to more than double SEG’s locally produced audio, television, and digital content across South Australia.

Sports Entertainment group CEO, Craig Hutchison, highlighted the value of combining prime CBD visibility with expanded local news and television production.

“South Australia is one of the great sporting states, and over the past eight years we’ve been incredibly proud of what SEG has built here.”

“From day one, our focus has been on giving South Australian sports fans a genuine home for the teams, competitions and conversations they care about, delivered by people who know and love sport in this state.

“SEN SA House is the next step in that commitment.

“We want to create something special in the heart of Adelaide; a place where people can walk past and see their favourite broadcasters in action, where we can produce outstanding content, and where fans feel connected to the sports they love.

“We’re making a significant investment in local jobs, talent and content production, creating new opportunities for South Australians to work in sports media and giving fans even more locally produced coverage,” Hutchison said.

Suncorp executive general manager – brand and customer experience, Mim Haysom, underscored AAMI’s deepening commercial and community footprint within South Australian sport.

“South Australia is an important part of AAMI’s story, and we’re proud to continue building our presence and connections with communities across the state.”

“Sport has a special way of bringing South Australians together.

“We’re looking forward to seeing SEN SA House become a destination for sports fans and a vibrant addition to the heart of Adelaide,” Hayson said.

The expansion creates dozens of new full-time and part-time media roles, establishing a dedicated South Australian news service alongside expanded syndication agreements with Gold 1323 AM and regional network Flow FM across its 12 stations. title: PGA Tour Sponsorship Revenue Tops $1 Billion As Rival LIV Fades
article_text:
The PGA Tour crossed a major financial milestone, as sponsorship revenue topped $1 billion for the first time. Mundo Deportivo reported the U.S.-based circuit saw a 14% increase in commercial income this year. This figure marks a new high for the organization after years of battling for control of professional golf.

Strong partnerships with global brands drove this growth. Rolex renewed its multiyear deal to remain the official timekeeper across all tour platforms, according to Mundo Deportivo. Alongside Rolex, agreements with Amazon Web Services, Raymond James, and AbbVie added significant weight to the revenue total.

The tour is using this money to fund a major structural shift starting in 2028. The schedule will split into two distinct groups: the Championship Series and the Challenger Series. The top tier will feature about 130 players in 24 events, each with a minimum prize purse of $20 million. Players will have a defined route upward as the lower tier organizes 20 events featuring purses no less than $4 million. Dhruv Prasad, the PGA Tour's chief commercial officer, stated the organization has secured deals for almost every future Championship Series tournament.

Prasad believes the market response validates this direction. He mentioned that discussions are underway with multiple firms regarding partnerships for the Challenger Series. This structure aims to create more stability for sponsors and players alike.

Not every long-standing relationship is guaranteed to continue. FedEx, which has exclusively sponsored the FedEx Cup since 2007, has not confirmed whether its deal will continue beyond 2027. As the tour redirects its attention, the partnership remains under examination. The tour cannot rely solely on legacy sponsors to fund its future growth.

Meanwhile, the rival LIV Golf circuit is fading fast. The Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund-backed group has begun shutting down after failing to relaunch its business. This collapse removes the primary threat that kept the PGA Tour on edge for five years. Strategic Sports Group has provided $1.5 billion in investment to the tour, funds that remain unspent. Those funds could improve facilities, hospitality, and ticketing operations.

The extended partnership with Rolex underscores the enduring appeal of the sport's history. The brand's connection to golf predates the 2005 tour deal by nearly four decades. In 1967, the brand appointed Arnold Palmer, Jack Nicklaus, and Gary Player as its first golf Testimonees. Today, active stars like Scottie Scheffler, Brooks Koepka, and Justin Thomas carry that same status. The tour commands premium rates from advertisers.

title: Galo announces Sólides sponsorship for the Copa Sul-Americana final

title: Australian media watchdog presses TV networks to curb sports alcohol ads
article_text:
Australia’s media regulator has called on the free-to-air TV sector to take “immediate steps” to lower children’s exposure to alcohol ads and remove exemptions allowing them to be shown during sports broadcasts.

Under current rules, direct alcohol adverts on terrestrial free-to-air television are restricted to overnight hours, from 8:30 pm to 5:00 am, and a midday window, from 12:00 pm to 3:00 pm on school days.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

However, exemptions apply to sports programmes broadcast on weekends and public holidays, as well as qualifying live sports broadcasts shown across multiple markets.

The Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA) has recommended that industry body Free TV Australia remove those exemptions.

ACMA chair Nerida O’Loughlin said: “These exemptions are unique to Australia and inconsistent with advertising of other restricted products, such as gambling.”

The media watchdog began a review in March to assess whether the existing rules provide “appropriate community safeguards” for television audiences.

It said its review found “widespread concern” about alcohol advertising and recognised a link between such advertising, increased consumption, and “risky drinking”.

The review also found that alcohol advertising on television represents a “relatively small” but “important” source of revenue for broadcasters.

The ACMA has also asked Free TV Australia to “voluntarily apply” the Free TV Code to television content provided through broadcasters’ online services.

If Free TV Australia does not submit a revised code for registration that provides appropriate community safeguards, the ACMA could determine a programme standard, it said.

Separate standards prohibit alcohol advertising before, during, and after children’s programmes. Cross-media industry codes also require adverts shown without age-gating to reach audiences expected to comprise at least 80% adults.

The ACMA has recommended that the Australian Government conduct a “holistic review” of alcohol advertising across all media.

“Our review found strong concerns about exposure to alcohol advertising through other media including online, at sporting venues, on jerseys and in other forms that all fall outside the ACMA’s remit.

“As a result, the ACMA has recommended that the Australian Government consider alcohol advertising regulation holistically, including looking at potential gaps and inconsistencies across platforms,” O’Loughlin said.

News: NHL media rights, Paramount-WBD, Angels and more
article_text:
The NHL has reportedly approached ESPN and TNT Sports about media rights renewals; Paramount has updated aspects of its hostile tender offer for Warner Bros. Discovery; and in-market streaming of Los Angeles Angels broadcasts will take place through the MLB DTC platform. Plus news on ESPN, Netflix, CBS-UFC and Fubo.

NHL commissioner Gary Bettman is said to have approached ESPN and TNT Sports about expediting their media rights negotiations, according to John Ourand of Puck Tuesday night. Ourand, who reported the same about the PGA Tour, wrote that the networks do not appear poised to negotiate new deals “until they know how much the NFL will ask for.” The NFL currently receives a reported sum of more than $11 billion annually for its media rights.

The NHL’s U.S. media rights deals, which are reportedly worth a combined $625 million, are not due to expire until after the 2028 season. But with the NFL widely expected to move up its media rights negotiations, leagues are reportedly looking to rush to the negotiating table while the networks still have money to spend.

TNT Sports lost its domestic NBA media rights package last year, but has in recent years acquired French Open tennis, NASCAR and — via sublicense — College Football Playoff games, among other properties. ESPN has committed billions in new rights and renewals since reacquiring NHL rights in March 2021 after a 17-year hiatus.

The NHL last year signed a 12-year media rights extension with Rogers Communications in Canada worth $11 billion CDN, but it does not begin until the 2026-27 season. Between the United States and Canada, the league will bring in reported media revenue of more than $1.2 billion USD per year for the two seasons those deals overlap.

Paramount on Tuesday updated its hostile tender offer for all of Warner Bros. Discovery to cover the $2.8 billion termination fee WBD would need to pay to get out of its commitment with Netflix, and add a $0.25/share “ticking fee” to WBD shareholders for every quarter the deal is not closed. The latter equates to approximately $650 million in cash value that would be distributed among WBD shareholders per quarter. Paramount again expressed confidence in quickly receiving the necessary regulatory approvals for the proposed transaction, which the company first initiated with a series of unsolicited bids starting last fall.

Paramount had previously sweetened its deal by raising the reverse termination fee to $5.8 billion, which is equivalent to the Netflix figure. Either of these suitors would need to compensate WBD with this fee if their pact does not receive regulatory approval. In its “enhanced” tender offer, Paramount claimed it would “fully reimburse” WBD for the potential $1.5 billion cost affiliated with not completing debt refinancing. The company said this payment would not reduce the reverse termination fee.

Paramount, which extended the expiration date for its offer by 10 days to March 2, has secured $43.6 billion in equity commitments coming from both the Ellison family and RedBird Capital Partners, including an “irrevocable personal guarantee” from Larry Ellison. Paramount also has $54 billion in debt commitments from Apollo, Bank of America and Citigroup. Moreover, Paramount said its financing sources would extend the maturity on a $15 billion bridge loan or that the company would “permit WBD to structure permanent financing in any way it chooses so long as the debt is redeemable at a commercially reasonable cost.”

Paramount has continued to argue that its bid is “superior” to the Netflix agreement, claiming the latter is operating off a sliding scale based on the amount of debt to be carried by Discovery Global. WBD disclosed that Discovery Global would carry $17 billion of debt “as of June 30, 2026” with a goal to reduce that number to $16.1 billion by year’s end. Since WBD is able to determine the amount of debt Discovery will hold prior to pro rata common stock distribution, a “debt adjustment mechanism” in the Netflix deal could potentially reduce its value. WBD confirmed receipt of Paramount’s offer, which its board will review.

The Los Angeles Angels on Tuesday joined the list of 21 Major League Baseball teams whose games will be distributed digitally via the league’s in-house direct-to-consumer platform, but it remains to be seen whether the team’s games will be produced by the league. The Angels are co-owners of the FanDuel Sports Network West RSN and are “contemplating buying out Main Street to launch their own network,” per a report by Mike Mazzeo of Sports Business Journal. Mazzeo cited sources who explained that the team has not ruled out launching a linear network this season or in the future, which could also include Los Angeles Kings NHL games.

While the majority of teams are working with MLB on the distribution of their games, not all of them are utilizing the league for production. At the moment, MLB is slated to produce live game broadcasts for the five teams it worked with last season (Diamondbacks, Guardians, Rockies, Twins, Padres) in addition to eight teams previously part of the Main Street Sports Group portfolio (Reds, Tigers, Royals, Marlins, Brewers, Cardinals, Rays, Nationals). The Seattle Mariners organization is also working with the league on production and distribution of local games after shutting down ROOT Sports Northwest last year.

For the 14 teams whose games are being both produced and distributed by MLB, the in-market streaming price is $20/month and $100 for the season. While the Angels have not announced their production arrangements for the upcoming season, the pricing is the same. MLB is also distributing local games televised on RSNs for six teams this season as well (Athletics, Orioles, Dodgers, Mets, Phillies, Giants). The pricing for these packages differs by market, and some of the solutions also include access to other programming from the applicable RSN.

title: Sid Lee Sport partners with Guinness to measure the true commercial value of sports sponsorship
article_text:
Major evaluation project spans six markets and nine rights holders, moving beyond traditional media valuation to assess the business impact of Guinness’s global sponsorship portfolio.

Global sports marketing agency Sid Lee Sport, working alongside sister agency, Kepler, is undertaking a major evaluation of Guinness’s global sports sponsorship portfolio, designed to establish a clearer understanding of the commercial impact of its football and rugby partnerships.

The project covers six key markets – Great Britain, Ireland, Kenya, the United States, Indonesia and South Korea – and nine rights holders, including the Premier League, Arsenal, Aston Villa, Newcastle United, the Guinness Men’s and Women’s Six Nations and the four home rugby unions.

Sid Lee Sport and Kepler’s combined evaluation uses KIP, a custom-built, proprietary intelligence platform, to analyse three years of sales, brand and partnership data, helping isolate the incremental commercial impact of Guinness’s sponsorship investments.

The analysis goes beyond exposure, examining broadcast media value, digital reach, stadium pouring rights, fan research and experiential activation, alongside how effectively each partnership is utilised across different markets.

The evaluation aims to provide Guinness with a consistent, commercially grounded understanding of sponsorship performance across markets and partners, helping inform future investment decisions and identify opportunities to unlock greater value from its portfolio.

Mike Grumbridge, Managing Director at Sid Lee Sport, said: “The sponsorship industry continues to rely heavily on traditional metrics such as media exposure and reach to demonstrate value, but that doesn’t necessarily tell brands what their investment is delivering commercially.

“Our work with Guinness is about going much further. By combining the proprietary intelligence model of Sid Lee Sport and Kepler with deep sponsorship expertise, we’re building a clearer picture of where sponsorship creates genuine business value and how brands can unlock more of it.

“We believe this represents an important step forward in how sponsorship effectiveness is understood and measured.”

“Guinness is a brand steeped in sporting heritage and renowned for its innovation. Working with Sid Lee Sport has helped us deﬁne how we shape our brand in sport,” said Paddy Carberry, Guinness Global Marketing Manager, Head of Sport.

The Guinness project reﬂects Sid Lee Sport’s wider commitment to helping brands unlock more value from sport, bringing together world-class creativity, deep sponsorship expertise and a focus on effectiveness.

On November 10 Sid Lee Sport and Guinness will host From Pitch to Pint, a live Unofﬁcial Partner podcast at its London headquarters, bringing together representatives from the brand and agency to explore the true value of sponsorship.
